study: Stage 2 of the paid-data decision: does Nasdaq order-book depth (information the desk has never seen) predict short-term direction in desk-like names well enough to beat the spread?
registered_at: 2026-10-04, before any depth data was bought or fetched
amended: 2026-10-04, before any data, after the result-skeptic pre-registration review (FIX FIRST): the original desk-fill sample (~36 gated signals in the test half) could not detect +5 bp, so a pass was impossible and a fail meaningless. Redesigned: large systematic random-entry sample is primary; desk fills secondary with no pass bar; H1 alone decides; signal time is never a fill; book read by ts_recv; 35 s window; within-name-day OBI; explicit feature rules.

data.source: Databento XNAS.ITCH (Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH), schema mbp-10; Nasdaq's book for every NMS name traded there (all listings), historical, pay-as-you-go against the $125 new-account credit
data.budget_guard: price the full request list with Databento metadata.get_cost before any download; abort if > $100. If the full sample does not fit, shrink sessions (never per-day sampling) and report the power the shrunk sample has before running
data.key: the user's Databento API key in a new file config/secrets.json.databento on the mini (gitignored by secrets.json.*); never printed or logged
data.universe: per session, the 40 largest gappers (open >= $10, prior-day dollar volume >= $20M, gap >= +2%) from the all-symbol daily panel, the same rule as the SIP breakout study
data.sessions: the 60 sessions 2026-06-01..2026-08-28 (before the desk's recorded fills; no overlap with any study that chose a parameter here)
data.primary_sample: 2 random entry minutes per name per session in 09:45-15:30 (seed 17) -> ~4,800 entries, ~2,400 per half
data.secondary_sample: desk entries >= $10 since 2026-09-16 (hold_days < 1, deduplicated), signal time = the first buy submit in ai_reports/fills/DAY.jsonl (never the fill); no pass bar, information only
data.windows: mbp-10 from signal - 35 s to signal (nothing after the signal is used)
data.tape: outcomes from the SIP tape: buy at the SIP ask at signal + 0.5 s (latency), sell at the SIP bid at signal + 0.5 s + H (exec_report.nbbo_at); never paper fills

features_at_signal.book_time: the last mbp-10 record with ts_recv <= signal (never ts_event); a 1 s guard (ts_recv <= signal - 1 s) is run as a sensitivity check because the mini's clock offset is unmeasured
features_at_signal.OBI5: (sum of bid sizes at the top 5 levels - sum of ask sizes) / their total
features_at_signal.OBI5_dm: OBI5 minus the mean OBI5 of that name's entries that session (so the gate cannot become a name/depth filter); PRIMARY form
features_at_signal.ASK_THIN30: ask depth over the top 5 levels at the signal / its TIME-WEIGHTED mean over the 30 s before, minus 1 (information)
features_at_signal.drops: drop and count an entry when: fewer than 5 levels on either side, a crossed or locked book, no book update in the 30 s before the signal, or a halt inside the window

outcome.primary_horizon: H = 120 s (the desk's median hold is ~100 s)

procedure: the OBI5_dm top-tercile cut-off is fixed on the FIRST half and applied unchanged to the second half

hypotheses.H1_PRIMARY: random entries in the top OBI5_dm tercile earn more over H = 120 s than the rest
hypotheses.H2_info: ASK_THIN30 bottom tercile (asks draining): information only; if it alone looks strong it is 'unconfirmed, needs a new held-out period'
hypotheses.H3_info: OBI1; 60/300 s; the desk-fill secondary sample; strata by listing exchange (Nasdaq-listed vs other) and by name

statistic: mean bp per entry, t clustered by day
pass: H1 alone decides. In the SECOND half: (a) gated minus rest >= +5 bp with day-clustered t >= 2; (b) the gated entries' own net > 0 after the spread they paid; (c) gated n >= 600; (d) the 1 s-guard sensitivity keeps (a) at t >= 1.5. Power check before reading the result: with the first-half per-entry sd, (c) must make +5 bp detectable at t = 2; if not, the run is declared underpowered and no verdict is drawn.
if_pass: result-skeptic review of the positive, then a firm quote for LIVE Nasdaq depth (exchange fees differ from historical), then a paper A/B with live depth; no live money on this result alone
if_fail: Nasdaq depth is not worth buying as an entry gate at the desk's ~2-minute horizon (only if the power check is met); other horizons are not covered
prior: low (~10-20%): book imbalance is known to predict seconds-scale mid moves usually smaller than the spread; the desk acts on 0.25-2 s ticks via IEX quotes and REST orders
caveats: Nasdaq-only book, not consolidated depth (a live gate would buy the same feed)
random entries stand in for the desk's entries, which test as noise-equivalent to random minutes
